$comment: GH-642 (queue item 6, stage 0b) - THE ONE LIST OF WHAT A CALCULATION NEEDS.
The owner's decision, 23.09.2026: 'there will be a list of the input parameters we
need for the calculation. The wizard will look at it, the calculation will look at
it, so that we do not put different checks in different places.'
ONE FILE, ONE READER. The server reads this; the wizard, Settings, the run and the
incomplete-run panel get it parsed, the way `analysis-result.schema.json` is already
read by the server and never copied into `assets`. A second list is the drift this
file exists to remove.
WHAT IS NOT HERE, AND DELIBERATELY:
- 'what breaks without it'. Who reads an input is what the dependency graph says;
restating it here would be a second answer to that question.
- the readings of a sample, one by one. Their names are declared once, by the lab
name map (`sample-manager.js`, `readingKeysFor`); an entry points at it.
- anything derived rather than asked: the climate regime, the purpose, the time
zone, the effective species. Those are named in `derived` below so the equality
test can exclude them BY NAME, with a reason, instead of by a rule.
`required: null` MEANS THE OWNER HAS NOT DECIDED, and it travels with `decision`.
It is not a guess and not a default: a warning built from this list stays silent
about such an input until she answers.
Contents drafted by the analyst (`PLAN-calculation-inputs-RU.md`, sections 14 and
14a) from a reading of the tree and the database, 22-24.09.2026.

$commentWhenAbsent: GH-749 (queue item 3ay) - WHAT THE ABSENCE OF A READING COSTS, declared beside the reading
rather than written into each module that meets it. A pair is {input, effect}: the key is one
of the read spellings this entry already declares, and each effect is one thing that does not
happen without it. The guard holds the pairs the code records against these, both ways -- a
pair recorded and not declared is red, and a pair declared that no module records is red --
and every declared pair has a case that runs the module and reads the pair back.
THESE ARE NOT THE WORDS A CLIENT READS. They name the effect for a reader of the run's own
record; the sentence a person sees is the owner's and is a separate question.
AND A PAIR SAYS WHAT IT DOES, NOT WHAT SOMETHING ELSE DOES. The pH pair used to read `the
phosphorus floor is not adjusted by pH`, which is a statement about how MLSN and SLAN behave -
parked as an open question by the owner's decision of 25.09.2026, and not this record's to
assert. The wording names the absence and the fact that a module recorded it; what any
methodology then does with a missing reading is that methodology's own subject.
A REQUIRED SETTING HAS NO PAIR HERE, and that is the analyst's decision rather than an
omission: `turf.methodology` has one owner and no allowed absence, so the resolver REFUSES
instead of recording an effect -- an effect would admit the case as an allowed one.

notInputs.soil.ESP: a result: worked out from the sodium and the CEC -- `assets/hub-tissue-v3.js` / `assessSoilSodium`

notInputs.pgr.gddThreshold: derived from the PGR product type, a property of the product rather than a question -- `assets/gilba-pgr-module-v3.js` / `w_pure`

notInputs.water.SAR: BOTH A LAB COLUMN AND A COMPUTED VALUE, measured under GH-712 and narrower than the reason written earlier the same night: a water report may carry SAR itself -- `assets/lab-import.js` / `SAR: { min: 0, max: 100, unit: '' }` -- and it is also computed from the ions where no column supplied it -- `assets/word-export.js` / `data.water.SAR = Na_meq`.
